findings.issue: Module-level `promise ??=` memoization caches rejected promises: one transient API failure permanently breaks the species index, generations, type list or home data for the session, with no retry or error surface (routes render bare <h1> fallbacks).
findings.suggestion: Use `cache()` from @solidjs/router (or clear the memoized promise on rejection) and render an explicit error state with a retry in each route's resource.

findings.issue: Pokémon moves section fans out one proxied fetch per move detail (~100 requests for a modern game), with no server-side aggregation and `cache-control: no-store` on the proxy (app/src/routes/api-proxy/[...path].ts:13), so every visitor and every game change re-downloads it all.
findings.suggestion: Let the proxy set a public max-age (data is a fixed snapshot per run) and/or aggregate move details server-side per request; at minimum raise the client TTL for immutable resources.

findings.issue: All fetch errors (502/500/timeout included) are swallowed into `return null`, which the routes render as 'Not found'; API downtime is indistinguishable from a missing resource.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish 404 from other statuses in ApiError and render a dedicated error view for non-404 failures.

findings.issue: No typecheck/lint scripts and no devDependencies; `strict: true` in app/tsconfig.json is never enforced because `tsc` never runs, and the data layer is ~30 `any`s deep.
findings.suggestion: Add a `typecheck: tsc --noEmit` script wired into CI, and type the main API payloads (pokemon, species, move) instead of `any`.

findings.issue: The 'build cards, exclude forms >10000, dedupe by id, sort' pipeline is duplicated three times (getMovePage, getAbilityPage, getTypePage), each rebuilding `speciesById`, with three different dedupe idioms including the `(seen.add(id), true)` comma trick.
findings.suggestion: Extract one `pokemonCards(refs)` helper in data.ts and share the speciesById map.

findings.issue: `typeLabel` — a type-name lookup — is used to label and sort *moves* on the type page, which only works by coincidence and diverges from the spec's 'sorted alphabetically by name'.
findings.suggestion: Use `humanize(move.name)` and sort by the API name.

findings.issue: `.map()` in JSX for options and card lists while `<For>` is used everywhere else; cards lose keying across page changes.
The hash-scroll effect re-fires on every moveData change, so changing the game select scrolls the user back to #moves.
findings.suggestion: Only scroll once per route navigation (key the effect on params.name), not on move-data refetches.

findings.issue: `document.documentElement.lang = "en"` as a top-level side effect duplicates the `lang="en"` already set in app/src/entry-server.tsx:10.
findings.suggestion: Delete the side effect; keep the lang attribute in the server document.

findings.issue: `ssr: false` (and the whole proxy-through-server data design) is a significant architecture choice left undocumented; the README is still the `npm init solid` template.
findings.suggestion: Either adopt SSR/`ssr: "data-only"` for a content site or record the rationale in the README.

summary: This is a competent, current-generation SolidStart v2 app — correct Vite 8 + nitro setup, file routing, sensible lib/component/route layering, and careful filter/pagination/sorting logic — that I'd merge after one round of changes. The main reservations are reliability, not structure: promise-level memoization that never retries, no error states (API failures masquerade as 'Not found'), and a chatty ~100-request fan-out for move tables through a no-store proxy. Consolidating the triplicated card pipeline, adding a typecheck script, and documenting the ssr:false/proxy decisions would make it a comfortable approve.
